question:
A concave spherical mirror has a radius of curvature of 30 cm. An object was placed 15 cm away from the pole in front of the mirror on the principal axis. Choose the correct option for the position, size and nature of the image formed, respectively.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options:
Behind the mirror, enlarged, virtual and erect

At infinity, highly enlarged, real and inverted

Between Focus and Centre, diminished, real and inverted

At the focus, highly diminished point-sized, real and inverted
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is At infinity, highly enlarged, real and inverted

Explanation:

The correct option is At infinity, highly enlarged, real and inverted.

Explanation
For the given concave spherical mirror, the radius of curvature is R=30 cm. The focal length (f) is half of the radius of curvature.

According to the Cartesian sign convention, for a concave mirror, the radius of curvature and focal length are negative.

Radius of Curvature, R=−30 cm

Focal Length, f=R/2=−30/2=−15 cm

The object is placed 15 cm in front of the mirror, so the object distance is u=−15 cm.

Since the object distance is equal to the focal length (u=f), the object is positioned at the principal focus of the mirror. When an object is placed at the focus of a concave mirror, the reflected rays become parallel to the principal axis and form an image at infinity. This image is highly enlarged, real, and inverted.



Extra Facts:
In a concave mirror, if the object is placed between the focus and the pole, the image is formed behind the mirror, virtual, erect, and enlarged. This property is used in shaving mirrors and magnifying glasses. The nature of the image in a concave mirror depends on the position of the object. If the object is placed beyond the focus, the image formed is real and inverted.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the relation between focal length and radius of curvature of a concave mirror? → f = R/2
☛ The image formed by a convex mirror is always? → Virtual, erect, and diminished
☛ Which mirror is used as a shaving mirror? → Concave mirror
☛ Reflection of light is governed by which law? → Angle of incidence = Angle of reflection
☛ Where is the image formed in a concave mirror when the object is at infinity? → At the focus
question_hi:
एक अवतल गोलाकार दर्पण की वक्रता त्रिज्या 30 cm है। एक वस्तु को मुख्य अक्ष पर दर्पण के सामने ध्रुव से 15 cm की दूरी पर रखा गया था । निर्मित प्रतिबिंब की क्रमश: स्थिति, आकार और प्रकृति के लिए सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi:
दर्पण के पीछे, विवर्धित, आभासी और सीधी

अनंत पर, अत्यधिक विवर्धित, वास्तविक और उल्टी

फोकस और केंद्र के बीच में, छोटी, वास्तविक और उल्टी

फोकस पर, अत्यधिक छोटे बिंदु-आकारीय, वास्तविक और उल्टी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अनंत पर, अत्यधिक विवर्धित, वास्तविक और उल्टी

Explanation:

सही विकल्प अनंत पर, अत्यधिक आवर्धित, वास्तविक और उल्टा है।

व्याख्या
दिए गए अवतल गोलीय दर्पण के लिए, वक्रता त्रिज्या R=30 सेमी है। फोकस दूरी (f) वक्रता त्रिज्या की आधी है।

कार्तीय चिह्न परिपाटी के अनुसार, अवतल दर्पण के लिए, वक्रता त्रिज्या और फोकस दूरी ऋणात्मक होती हैं।

वक्रता त्रिज्या, R=−30 सेमी

फोकस दूरी, f=R/2=−30/2=−15 सेमी

वस्तु दर्पण के सामने 15 सेमी की दूरी पर रखी गई है, इसलिए वस्तु की दूरी u=−15 सेमी है।

चूँकि वस्तु की दूरी फोकस दूरी (u=f) के बराबर है, इसलिए वस्तु दर्पण के मुख्य फोकस पर स्थित है। जब किसी वस्तु को अवतल दर्पण के फोकस पर रखा जाता है, तो परावर्तित किरणें मुख्य अक्ष के समानांतर हो जाती हैं और अनंत पर एक प्रतिबिम्ब बनाती हैं। यह छवि अत्यधिक विस्तृत, वास्तविक और उल्टी है।



Extra Facts:
अवतल दर्पण में, यदि वस्तु फोकस और ध्रुव के बीच रखी जाती है, तो प्रतिबिंब दर्पण के पीछे आभासी, सीधा और विवर्धित बनता है। यह दर्पण का उपयोग शेविंग मिरर और मैग्निफाइंग ग्लास के रूप में किया जाता है। अवतल दर्पण में प्रतिबिंब की प्रकृति वस्तु की स्थिति पर निर्भर करती है। यदि वस्तु फोकस से परे है, तो प्रतिबिंब वास्तविक और उल्टा बनता है।

question:
Which among the following represents the Lens formula?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1h+1v=1f
1v-1u=1f
1v+1f=1u
1v+1u=1f
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1v-1u=1f

Explanation:
The Lens Formula is a fundamental equation in optics that relates the image distance (v), object distance (u), and the focal length (f) of a lens. It is mathematically represented as 1/v - 1/u = 1/f. Here, u is always taken as negative because the object is placed on the left side of the lens (as per Cartesian sign convention). This formula is applicable to both convex and concave lenses, provided the sign convention is followed correctly.

Extra Facts:
The Lens Formula is derived from the Lens Maker's Formula and the laws of refraction. The focal length (f) depends on the curvature radius of the lens and its refractive index. A convex lens has a positive focal length, while a concave lens has a negative focal length. This formula is widely used in designing optical instruments like microscopes, telescopes, and camera lenses to determine image positions.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the focal length of a convex lens? → Positive
☛ What is the focal length of a concave lens? → Negative
☛ What is the speed of light in a vacuum? → 3 × 10^8 m/s
☛ Which lens is present in the human eye? → Convex lens
☛ What is the SI unit of lens power? → Diopter
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन लेंस सूत्र का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: 1h+1v=1f
1v-1u=1f
1v+1f=1u
1v+1u=1f
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 1v-1u=1f

Explanation:
लेंस सूत्र प्रकाशिकी में एक महत्वपूर्ण सूत्र है जो लेंस द्वारा बनाई गई छवि की स्थिति (v), वस्तु की स्थिति (u), और लेंस की फोकस दूरी (f) के बीच संबंध स्थापित करता है। यह सूत्र 1/v - 1/u = 1/f के रूप में लिखा जाता है। यहां, u हमेशा ऋणात्मक लिया जाता है क्योंकि वस्तु को लेंस के बाईं ओर रखा जाता है (कार्तीय चिह्न परिपाटी के अनुसार)। इस सूत्र का उपयोग उत्तल और अवतल दोनों प्रकार के लेंसों के लिए किया जा सकता है, बशर्ते चिह्न परिपाटी का सही ढंग से पालन किया जाए।

Extra Facts:
लेंस सूत्र का व्युत्पत्ति लेंस मेकर्स फॉर्मूला और अपवर्तन के नियमों पर आधारित है। फोकस दूरी (f) लेंस की वक्रता त्रिज्या और अपवर्तनांक पर निर्भर करती है। उत्तल लेंस की फोकस दूरी धनात्मक होती है, जबकि अवतल लेंस की ऋणात्मक। इस सूत्र का उपयोग माइक्रोस्कोप, टेलीस्कोप, कैमरा लेंस आदि में छवि की स्थिति निर्धारित करने के लिए किया जाता है।

question:
An image which cannot be obtained on a screen is called a__________

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: virtual image
real image
vector image
spectral image
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is virtual image

Explanation:
In optics, a virtual image is an image that cannot be obtained on a screen. It is formed by the apparent intersection of light rays, whereas a real image is formed by the actual intersection of light rays and can be projected on a screen. A virtual image is always erect and is formed behind the mirror or lens. For example, the image formed by a plane mirror is virtual.

Extra Facts:
A real image can be obtained on a screen because it is formed at the actual point of convergence of light rays. This image can be inverted. For example, the image formed by a concave mirror or convex lens can be real if the object is placed beyond the focus. Virtual images are used in devices like telescopes, microscopes, and other optical instruments.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the speed of light? → 3 × 10^8 m/s
☛ What type of image is formed by a plane mirror? → Virtual and erect
☛ When is the image formed by a concave mirror real? → When the object is placed beyond the focus
☛ What type of image is formed by a convex lens? → Virtual and erect (when the object is placed within the focus)
☛ Which law governs the reflection of light? → Angle of incidence = Angle of reflection
question_hi:
जिस प्रतिबिंब को पर्दे पर प्राप्त नहीं किया जा सकता है,___________ कहलाता है।

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: आभासी प्रतिबिंब
वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब
वेक्टर प्रतिबिंब
वर्णक्रमीय प्रतिबिंब
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है आभासी प्रतिबिंब

Explanation:
प्रकाशिकी में, आभासी प्रतिबिंब वह प्रतिबिंब होता है जिसे पर्दे पर प्राप्त नहीं किया जा सकता है। यह प्रतिबिंब प्रकाश किरणों के आभासी प्रतिच्छेदन से बनता है, जबकि वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब प्रकाश किरणों के वास्तविक प्रतिच्छेदन से बनता है और इसे पर्दे पर प्राप्त किया जा सकता है। आभासी प्रतिबिंब सदैव सीधा (erect) होता है और यह दर्पण या लेंस के पीछे बनता है। उदाहरण के लिए, समतल दर्पण में बना प्रतिबिंब आभासी होता है।

Extra Facts:
वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब को पर्दे पर प्राप्त किया जा सकता है क्योंकि यह प्रकाश किरणों के वास्तविक मिलन बिंदु पर बनता है। यह प्रतिबिंब उल्टा (inverted) हो सकता है। उदाहरण के लिए, अवतल दर्पण या उत्तल लेंस द्वारा बनाया गया प्रतिबिंब वास्तविक हो सकता है यदि वस्तु फोकस से दूर स्थित हो। आभासी प्रतिबिंब का उपयोग दूरबीन, माइक्रोस्कोप और अन्य ऑप्टिकल उपकरणों में किया जाता है।

question:
The _______ of a ray is the angle measured from the reflected ray to the normal surface.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Angle of Diffusion
Angle of Reflection
Angle of Incidence
Angle of Refraction
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Angle of Reflection

Explanation:
The angle of reflection is the angle between the reflected ray and the normal (a line perpendicular to the surface). When a light ray strikes a surface, it reflects off the surface. The angle of incidence (∠i) is the angle between the incident ray and the normal, while the angle of reflection (∠r) is the angle between the reflected ray and the normal. According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection (∠i = ∠r). This law is fundamental in understanding how light behaves when it reflects off surfaces like mirrors, lenses, etc.

Extra Facts:
There are two main types of reflection: regular reflection and diffuse reflection. In regular reflection, the surface is smooth, and all reflected rays travel in the same direction (e.g., mirrors). In diffuse reflection, the surface is rough, and reflected rays scatter in different directions (e.g., walls or paper). The laws of reflection are applied in devices like periscopes, cameras, and telescopes.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ How is an image formed in a mirror? → Due to the reflection of light
☛ What is the nature of the image in a plane mirror? → Virtual and erect
☛ How is the focal length of a concave mirror calculated? → f = R/2
☛ What is the sign of the focal length of a convex mirror? → Positive
question_hi:
________ किसी किरण का परावर्तित किरण से अभिलंब पृष्ठ पर मापा गया कोण है।

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options_hi: विसरण कोण
परावर्तन कोण
आपतन कोण
अपवर्तन कोण
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है परावर्तन कोण (Angle of Reflection)

Explanation:
परावर्तन कोण वह कोण है जो परावर्तित किरण और अभिलंब (normal) के बीच बनता है। जब प्रकाश की एक किरण किसी सतह पर आपतित होती है, तो वह परावर्तित होती है। आपतन कोण (angle of incidence) आपतित किरण और अभिलंब के बीच का कोण होता है, जबकि परावर्तन कोण परावर्तित किरण और अभिलंब के बीच का कोण होता है। परावर्तन के नियम के अनुसार, आपतन कोण हमेशा परावर्तन कोण के बराबर होता है (∠i = ∠r)। यह नियम प्रकाश के परावर्तन की मूलभूत व्याख्या करता है और दर्पणों, लेंसों आदि में प्रकाश के व्यवहार को समझने में मदद करता है।

Extra Facts:
प्रकाश के परावर्तन के दो मुख्य प्रकार हैं: नियमित परावर्तन (regular reflection) और विसरित परावर्तन (diffuse reflection)। नियमित परावर्तन में, सतह चिकनी होती है और सभी परावर्तित किरणें एक ही दिशा में जाती हैं, जैसे दर्पण में। विसरित परावर्तन में, सतह खुरदरी होती है और परावर्तित किरणें विभिन्न दिशाओं में बिखर जाती हैं, जैसे दीवार या कागज पर। परावर्तन के नियमों का उपयोग पेरिस्कोप, कैमरा, टेलीस्कोप आदि में किया जाता है।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

question:
Which among the following has its refractive index closest to that of crown glass ?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: Canada balsam
Sapphire
Diamond
Ruby
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Canada balsam

Explanation:
The refractive index of crown glass is approximately 1.52. Canada balsam has a refractive index of about 1.53-1.54, which is closest to that of crown glass. It is used in optical instruments to cement lenses together because it causes minimal deviation in light refraction. Sapphire (1.76-1.77), diamond (2.42), and ruby (1.76-1.77) have significantly higher refractive indices compared to crown glass.

Extra Facts:
Crown glass is a type of optical glass with low dispersion. It is a soda-lime silicate glass and is used in lenses, prisms, and other optical devices. Canada balsam is a natural resin that is transparent and sticky. It is used for mounting microscope slides and in optical experiments due to its refractive properties.

☛ What is the refractive index of crown glass? → ~1.52
☛ What is Canada balsam used for? → Cementing lenses
☛ What is the refractive index of air? → 1.0003
☛ What is the refractive index of water? → ~1.33
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से इसका अपवर्तनांक क्राउन ग्लास के सबसे निकट है ?

नीलम
हीरा

solution_hi:

Explanation:
क्राउन ग्लास का अपवर्तनांक लगभग 1.52 होता है। कनाडा बालसम का अपवर्तनांक भी लगभग 1.53-1.54 के बीच होता है, जो क्राउन ग्लास के सबसे निकट है। इसका उपयोग प्रकाशिक उपकरणों में लेंस को जोड़ने के लिए किया जाता है क्योंकि यह प्रकाश के अपवर्तन में कम विचलन पैदा करता है। नीलम (1.76-1.77), हीरा (2.42), और रूबी (1.76-1.77) का अपवर्तनांक क्राउन ग्लास की तुलना में काफी अधिक होता है।

Extra Facts:

question:
Raman wants to use a rear-view mirror in his vehicle. Which type of mirror should he pick for it ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Convex Mirrors
Plane Mirrors
Cylindrical Mirrors
Concave Mirrors
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Convex Mirrors

Explanation:
Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they provide a wide field of view. The outward curvature of convex mirrors makes objects appear smaller (diminished) but covers a larger area. This allows the driver to see a broader view of the rear, enhancing driving safety. Plane mirrors offer a limited view, while concave mirrors magnify objects but reduce the field of view. Hence, convex mirrors are the most suitable for safety purposes.

Extra Facts:
Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images. They are used not only in vehicles but also at road turns, shopping malls, and hospitals for surveillance of large areas. The focal length of a convex mirror is positive, and it diverges light. In contrast, concave mirrors converge light and can form real and inverted images. Convex mirrors are also known as diverging mirrors.

☛ Where are concave mirrors used? → Shaving mirrors, telescopes, solar cookers
☛ What type of image is formed by a plane mirror? → Virtual, erect, and same-sized
☛ Which mirror has a negative focal length? → Concave mirror
☛ Which mirror is used in side-view mirrors? → Convex mirror

रमन अपने वाहन में पश्च-हृश्य दर्पण का प्रयोग करना चाहता है। इसके लिए उसे किस प्रकार का दर्पण चुनना चाहिए?

समतल दर्पण
बेलनाकार दर्पण
अवतल दर्पण
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है उत्तल दर्पण

Explanation:
पश्च-हृश्य दर्पण (Rear-view mirror) के रूप में उत्तल दर्पण का उपयोग किया जाता है क्योंकि यह एक विस्तृत क्षेत्र (वाइड फील्ड ऑफ़ व्यू) प्रदान करता है। उत्तल दर्पण की वक्रता बाहर की ओर होती है, जिसके कारण यह वस्तुओं को छोटा (सिकुड़ा हुआ) दिखाता है, लेकिन अधिक क्षेत्र को कवर करता है। यह ड्राइवर को वाहन के पीछे का व्यापक दृश्य देता है, जिससे सुरक्षित ड्राइविंग में मदद मिलती है। समतल दर्पण सीमित दृश्य प्रदान करते हैं, जबकि अवतल दर्पण वस्तुओं को बड़ा दिखाते हैं, लेकिन क्षेत्र कम होता है। इसलिए, सुरक्षा के लिए उत्तल दर्पण सबसे उपयुक्त होते हैं।

Extra Facts:
उत्तल दर्पण हमेशा आभासी, सीधा और छोटा प्रतिबिंब बनाते हैं। इनका उपयोग न केवल वाहनों में बल्कि सड़कों के मोड़ों, शॉपिंग मॉल्स और अस्पतालों में भी किया जाता है ताकि बड़े क्षेत्र को देखा जा सके। उत्तल दर्पण की फोकस दूरी धनात्मक होती है और यह प्रकाश को अपसारित (Diverge) करता है। इसके विपरीत, अवतल दर्पण प्रकाश को अभिसारित (Converge) करते हैं और वास्तविक तथा उल्टा प्रतिबिंब बना सकते हैं।

question:
________are formed when an opaque object comes in the path of light.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Mirror reflections
Shadows
Translucent rays
Transparent rays
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shadows

Explanation:
When an opaque object comes in the path of light, it completely blocks the light, resulting in the formation of a shadow. A shadow is a dark area where light cannot reach. This phenomenon is based on the principle of 'rectilinear propagation of light', which states that light travels in a straight line. The size and direction of the shadow depend on the position of the light source and the shape of the object. This can be easily observed in daily life, such as the formation of our shadow when standing in sunlight.

Extra Facts:
Shadows are of two types: Umbra (complete darkness) and Penumbra (partial darkness). The umbra is the region where light is completely blocked, while the penumbra is where light is partially blocked. Shadows play a significant role in eclipses. During a solar eclipse, the Moon's shadow falls on Earth, blocking the Sun. Similarly, during a lunar eclipse, Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. Shadows are also used in various applications like sundials and shadow puppetry.

question:
In optics, which term refers to the opening of the diaphragm of a lens that spatially limits the propagation of light ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: Collimator
Aperture
Apostilb
Meniscus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Aperture

Explanation:
In optics, Aperture refers to the opening of the diaphragm of a lens that spatially limits the propagation of light. It is a hole or an opening through which light passes. The size of the aperture affects the amount of light and the depth of field of the image. A smaller aperture allows less light to pass and results in a greater depth of field, while a larger aperture allows more light to pass and results in a shallower depth of field. It plays a crucial role in cameras, telescopes, and other optical devices.

Extra Facts:
1. Aperture is usually expressed by the f-number, such as f/2.8, f/4, etc. It is the ratio of the lens's focal length to the diameter of the aperture.
2. Collimator is a device that makes light rays parallel, while Meniscus is a type of lens with one convex and one concave surface.
3. Aperture is also used in astronomical telescopes to gather more light and obtain better images.

question:
White light is an example of:

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: laser light
plane polarised light
monochromatic light
polychromatic light
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is polychromatic light

Explanation:
White light is an example of polychromatic light because it consists of multiple wavelengths of light. When white light passes through a prism, it disperses into different colors (wavelengths) such as violet, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red. This dispersion occurs because each color has a specific wavelength and is refracted at a different angle by the prism. Thus, white light is not monochromatic (single color) but a mixture of many colors.

Extra Facts:
1. Isaac Newton was the first to demonstrate the dispersion of white light using a prism, a phenomenon known as 'dispersion of light'.
2. Monochromatic light consists of a single wavelength, such as laser light.
3. Polarised light is light in which vibrations occur in a single plane.

question:
What is the color of the light emitted by the Sun ?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: Yellow
Orange
Red
White
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is White

Explanation:
The light emitted by the Sun is actually white. It is a mixture of all colors (different wavelengths), which we call the spectrum. When this light passes through Earth's atmosphere, Rayleigh scattering causes blue light to scatter more, making the sky appear blue and the Sun appear yellow or orange. However, in reality, sunlight is white, containing all colors (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet).

Extra Facts:
- Sunlight is part of the electromagnetic spectrum, which includes visible light as well as infrared and ultraviolet rays.
- A prism can split white light into its component colors, a phenomenon called dispersion.
- Sunlight takes 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth because the speed of light is approximately 3 × 108 m/s.

question:
What is the main sense organ that virtual reality displays are aiming for?

Explanation:
Virtual Reality (VR) displays primarily target the vision sense. VR technology uses a headset or display device that presents a 3D computer-generated environment in front of the user's eyes. This technology works on the principle of binocular vision, where each eye is shown a slightly different image to create a sense of depth (stereopsis), making the experience feel realistic. VR also employs eye-tracking and high-resolution displays to enhance immersion and provide a lifelike experience.

Extra Facts:
1. VR technology uses stereoscopic displays, which present two separate images to create a 3D effect.
2. Apart from VR, Augmented Reality (AR) is also vision-based but overlays digital elements onto the real world.
3. Among human sensory organs, vision is the most information-rich, which is why VR technology focuses on it.

question:
What is the SI unit of power of a lens called?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Presbyopic.
Myopic
Dioptre
Hypermetropia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dioptre

Explanation:
The power of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length (f). It is expressed by the formula:
[ P = frac{1}{f} ]
Here, if the focal length is in meters (m), the SI unit of lens power is Dioptre (D). 1 Dioptre is equal to the power of a lens with a focal length of 1 meter. This unit is also used to measure the power of corrective lenses (e.g., for myopia, hypermetropia).

Extra Facts:
• The term Dioptre is derived from the Greek word 'dioptra,' an ancient optical instrument.
• A convex lens has a positive (+) power, while a concave lens has a negative (-) power.
• Optometrists use this unit to prescribe eyeglass lenses.

☛ What is the power of a concave lens? → Negative (-)

यहाँ, यदि फोकस दूरी मीटर (m) में है, तो लेंस की क्षमता का SI मात्रक डायोप्टर (D) होता है। 1 डायोप्टर उस लेंस की क्षमता के बराबर होता है जिसकी फोकस दूरी 1 मीटर हो। यह मात्रक नेत्र संबंधी दोषों (जैसे मायोपिया, हाइपरमेट्रोपिया) के सुधार के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले लेंस की क्षमता को मापने में भी प्रयोग किया जाता है।

question:
The blue colour of the sky is due to the:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Dispersion of light
Scattering of light
Refraction of light
Diffraction of light
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Scattering of light

Explanation:
The blue colour of the sky is due to the scattering of light. When sunlight enters the Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and dust particles present in the atmosphere. According to Rayleigh's Scattering Law, the shorter the wavelength of light, the more it is scattered. Blue light has a shorter wavelength (approximately 450-495 nm) compared to other colours, so it is scattered the most, making the sky appear blue.

Extra Facts:
Rayleigh's Scattering Law states that the intensity of scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength of light (I ∝ 1/λ⁴). During sunrise and sunset, the sky appears red or orange because sunlight has to pass through a thicker layer of the atmosphere, and blue light is scattered away, while red light, which is less scattered, reaches our eyes directly.

☛ According to Rayleigh's Scattering Law, scattering is inversely proportional to what? → Fourth power of wavelength
☛ Why does the ocean appear blue? → Due to the reflection of the sky and scattering of light
☛ How is a rainbow formed? → Due to dispersion and refraction of light
☛ Which colour of light has the shortest wavelength? → Violet
question_hi:
आकाश का नीला रंग किसके कारण होता है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: प्रकाश का वर्ण विक्षेपण
प्रकाश का प्रकीर्णन
प्रकाश का अपवर्तन
प्रकाश का विवर्तन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है प्रकाश का प्रकीर्णन

Explanation:
आकाश का नीला रंग प्रकाश के प्रकीर्णन (Scattering of light) के कारण होता है। जब सूर्य का प्रकाश पृथ्वी के वायुमंडल में प्रवेश करता है, तो यह वायुमंडल में मौजूद गैसों के अणुओं और धूल के कणों से टकराता है। रेले के प्रकीर्णन नियम (Rayleigh Scattering) के अनुसार, प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य जितनी कम होगी, उसका प्रकीर्णन उतना ही अधिक होगा। नीले रंग की तरंगदैर्ध्य (लगभग 450-495 nm) अन्य रंगों की तुलना में कम होती है, इसलिए यह सबसे अधिक प्रकीर्णित होता है और आकाश नीला दिखाई देता है।

Extra Facts:

question:
Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum wavelength?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Violet
Yellow
Green
Red
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Violet

Explanation:
VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) represents the seven colors of the visible light spectrum. Among these, violet light has the shortest wavelength (approximately 400-450 nm), while red light has the longest wavelength (approximately 620-750 nm). The relationship between wavelength (λ) and frequency (ν) is given by c = νλ (where c is the speed of light). Since violet has the shortest wavelength, it has the highest frequency. This property plays a crucial role in phenomena like scattering (e.g., why the sky appears blue) and refraction (e.g., dispersion by a prism).

Extra Facts:
1. Rayleigh Scattering Law states that the scattering of light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of its wavelength (I ∝ 1/λ⁴). Hence, violet light scatters the most, but the sky appears blue because blue light (also short-wavelength) dominates human vision.
2. A prism separates light into its constituent colors based on wavelength, with violet deviating the most.
3. Ultraviolet (UV) rays have even shorter wavelengths than violet and are invisible to the human eye.

question:
The total number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at 120° to each other is ______.

[SSC CGL 2019]
options:
1

2

4

3
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2

Explanation:
When two mirrors are inclined at an angle θ, the number of images formed is calculated by the formula:
n = (360° / θ) - 1
For θ = 120°:
n = (360° / 120°) - 1 = 3 - 1 = 2
This formula applies only if 360° is exactly divisible by θ. If not, the number of images may be infinite.

Extra Facts:
◼ A smaller angle between mirrors increases the number of images. For example, mirrors at 60° form 5 images.
◼ Parallel mirrors (θ = 0°) create infinite images due to repeated reflections.
◼ This principle is used in kaleidoscopes to generate colorful patterns.

question:

options: Kerosene – 1.44

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Benzene – 2.42

Explanation:
The Refractive Index (n) is the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in a medium. It depends on the density of the medium and the bending of light. Among the given options, Benzene has a refractive index of 1.50, not 2.42. The other pairs are correct: Kerosene (1.44), Sapphire (1.77), and Ruby (1.71). Thus, the pair Benzene-2.42 is incorrect.

Extra Facts:
The Refractive Index is a dimensionless quantity denoted by 'n'. It indicates the medium's ability to bend light. Diamond has the highest refractive index (2.42), which makes it sparkle. Water has a refractive index of 1.33, and glass is around 1.5. The refractive index also depends on temperature and the wavelength of light.

question:
Shadows are formed when ____ objects come in the path of light.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: translucent
transparent
luminous
opaque
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is opaque

Explanation:
Shadows are formed when opaque objects obstruct the path of light. Opaque objects completely block light, either by absorbing or reflecting it, creating a region of darkness (shadow) behind them. Transparent objects (e.g., glass) allow light to pass through completely, while translucent objects (e.g., frosted glass) scatter light partially but do not form clear shadows. Luminous objects emit their own light and thus do not cast shadows.

Extra Facts:
Understanding light behavior is crucial in physics. Light travels in straight lines, known as rectilinear propagation. The formation of shadows depends on the position of the light source, the object, and the screen. Opaque materials like wood, metal, or thick cloth can create shadows. The size of the shadow varies with the distance between the light source and the object. Shadows are used in various applications, such as sundials and shadow puppetry.

question:
If a lens has a focal length of 25 cm, what will be the power of that lens?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 4D
2D
1D
6D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 4D

Explanation:
The power (P) of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length (f). The formula is:
P = 1/f
Where P is in diopters (D) and f must be in meters (m).
Given: f = 25 cm = 0.25 m
Thus,
P = 1/0.25 = 4 D
Therefore, the power of the lens is 4D.

Extra Facts:
1. The unit of lens power is diopter (D).
2. A convex lens has a positive focal length, while a concave lens has a negative focal length.
3. The higher the power of a lens, the greater the refraction of light rays.
4. The human eye lens has a power of approximately 16D to 20D, which can adjust accordingly.

4. Gold and copper happen to absorb ______ and violet light, leaving yellow light.

Explanation:
Gold (Au) and copper (Cu) metals absorb blue and violet light while reflecting yellow light. This is due to their unique electronic structure. When light falls on these metals, the energy of blue and violet light is absorbed by electrons, while yellow light is reflected. This is why gold and copper appear yellow. This phenomenon is based on the principle of light absorption and reflection, where metals interact differently with light of varying wavelengths.

Extra Facts:

question:
The center of the reﬂecting surface of a spherical mirror is a point called:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: principal axis
pole
center of curvature
focus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pole

Explanation:
The center of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called the 'Pole'. It is the point on the principal axis where the reflecting surface begins. The pole is denoted by 'P' and plays a crucial role in determining the radius of curvature and focus of the mirror. All measurements related to the spherical mirror, such as object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f), are taken from the pole.

Extra Facts:
• Spherical mirrors are of two types: concave and convex mirrors.
• Center of Curvature is the point at the center of the spherical surface from which the mirror is cut.
• Focus is the point where parallel rays converge (in concave mirrors) or appear to diverge (in convex mirrors) after reflection.
• The mirror formula for spherical mirrors is: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f = focal length, v = image distance, u = object distance.

question:
Which of the two colours of spectrum forms the extremes?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Violet and Red
Yellow and Orange
Blue and Green
Red and Orange
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Violet and Red

Explanation:
The spectrum of light consists of seven colors: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red. Among these, Violet has the shortest wavelength (approximately 400 nm), while Red has the longest wavelength (approximately 700 nm). Therefore, the two extremes of the spectrum are Violet and Red. This can be observed during the refraction of light, where Violet light bends the most and Red light bends the least.

Extra Facts:
The spectrum of light was discovered by Newton. The order of colors in the spectrum can be remembered by the acronym 'VIBGYOR' (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red). Violet light scatters the most, which is why the sky appears blue. Red light scatters the least, which is why the sky appears red during sunrise and sunset.

question:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are true regarding the light year?
1.Light year is a unit of distance.
2.Light is a unit of time.
3.A light year is the distance that light travels in one Earth year.
4.Light year is the measurement of light intensity.

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Only 1 is correct
Only 1 and 3 are correct
Only 2 is correct
Only 1 and 2 are correct
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only 1 and 3 are correct

Explanation:
A light year is a unit of distance used to measure astronomical distances. It represents the distance that light travels in one Earth year in a vacuum. The speed of light is approximately 3 × 108 m/s, and the distance covered by light in one year is about 9.46 × 1012 km.
- Statement 1 is correct because a light year is a unit of distance.
- Statement 3 is also correct as it defines the distance light travels in one Earth year.
- Statement 2 is incorrect because light is not a unit of time.
- Statement 4 is incorrect because a light year measures distance, not light intensity.

Extra Facts:
- The light year is used to measure distances between galaxies, stars, and other celestial objects.
- The nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.24 light years away from Earth.
- Our galaxy, the Milky Way, has a diameter of approximately 1,00,000 light years.
- In astronomy, parsec (pc) is another important unit of distance, equal to about 3.26 light years.

1. प्रकाश वर्ष, दूरी की इकाई है।
2. प्रकाश, समय की इकाई है।
3. प्रकाश वर्ष वह दूरी है, जो प्रकाश, एक पृथ्वी वर्ष में तय करता है।
4. प्रकाश वर्ष प्रकाश की तीव्रता का माप है।

[SSC CPO 2024]

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है केवल 1 और 3 सही हैं

Explanation:
प्रकाश वर्ष (Light Year) एक दूरी की इकाई है, जिसका उपयोग खगोलीय दूरियों को मापने के लिए किया जाता है। यह वह दूरी है जो प्रकाश एक वर्ष में निर्वात (वैक्यूम) में तय करता है। प्रकाश की गति लगभग 3 × 108 मीटर/सेकंड होती है, और एक पृथ्वी वर्ष में प्रकाश द्वारा तय की गई दूरी लगभग 9.46 × 1012 किलोमीटर होती है।
- कथन 1 सही है क्योंकि प्रकाश वर्ष दूरी की इकाई है।
- कथन 3 भी सही है क्योंकि यह प्रकाश द्वारा एक वर्ष में तय की गई दूरी को परिभाषित करता है।
- कथन 2 गलत है क्योंकि प्रकाश समय की इकाई नहीं है।
- कथन 4 गलत है क्योंकि प्रकाश वर्ष प्रकाश की तीव्रता का माप नहीं है, बल्कि दूरी का माप है।

Extra Facts:
- प्रकाश वर्ष का उपयोग आकाशगंगाओं, तारों और अन्य खगोलीय पिंडों के बीच की दूरी मापने के लिए किया जाता है।
- निकटतम तारा प्रॉक्सिमा सेंटॉरी पृथ्वी से लगभग 4.24 प्रकाश वर्ष दूर है।
- हमारी आकाशगंगा, मिल्की वे, का व्यास लगभग 1,00,000 प्रकाश वर्ष है।
- खगोल विज्ञान में पारसेक (Parsec) भी एक महत्वपूर्ण दूरी की इकाई है, जो लगभग 3.26 प्रकाश वर्ष के बराबर होती है।
